ref: ch. 1 (Otto and ANF chapter numbers coincide; Otto marks '1.' at this paragraph)
greek: 1. "la δόγματι καὶ λόγῳ τῆς ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν ἀληϑείας dyo- μένῳ παραφύεταί τι ψεῦδος" ὃ παραφύεται δὲ οὐκ ἐξ ὑποκειμένης τινὸς ἀρχῆς κατὰ φύσιν ὁρμώμενον ἢ τῆς κατ᾽ αὐτὸ ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἕκαστον αἰτίας, ἀλλ᾽ ὑπὸ τῶν τὴν ἔκθεσμον σπορὰν ἐπὶ διαφθορᾷ τῆς ἀληϑείας τετιμηκότων σπουδαζόμενον.
greek_edition: Otto, Corpus Apologetarum Christianorum saeculi secundi vol. VII (Athenagoras), Jena 1857; read from the text layer of the archive.org scan (PDF p. 381, printed p. 186 inferred from the sequence of running heads; not legible on that page). OCR: 'la' stands for the lemma Παντὶ (apparatus line '2. Παντὶ δόγματι'); 'dyo-' is the line-break of ὁμολογουμένῳ; 'ϑ' is OCR for θ; accents as read by OCR, not checked against the printed letter.
english: By the side of every opinion and doctrine which agrees with the truth of things, there springs up some falsehood; and it does so, not because it takes its rise naturally from some fundamental principle, or from some cause peculiar to the matter in hand, but because it is invented on purpose by men who set a value on the spurious seed, for its tendency to corrupt the truth.
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe, Buffalo 1885), as posted at newadvent.org/fathers/0206.htm
edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII; scan reissued Wiesbaden: Martin Sändig 1969 (archive.org metadata)
what_it_says: The work opens by saying falsehood always grows up beside truth, sown on purpose by people who corrupt the truth.
limits: Says nothing about God's nature, the Logos or the Spirit; it is a methodological opening.

greek: Οὔτε γὰρ tal vonzal φύσεις ἐκ τῆς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀναστάσεως ἀδικηθεῖεν ἄν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐμπόδιόν τι ταύταις πρὸς τὸ εἶναι, οὐ δ βλάβος οὐχ ὕβρις ἡ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀνάστασις
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, text layer of archive.org scan, PDF p. 435 (printed p. 222, running head visible). OCR errors: 'tal vonzal' = αἱ νοηταὶ (Otto's own lemma on the same page is 'αἱ νοηταὶ φύσϑις'); 'οὐ δ βλάβος' = οὐδὲ βλάβος(?). Kept as read.
english: Spiritual natures (νοηταὶ φύσεις) cannot be injured by the resurrection of men, for the resurrection of men is no hindrance to their existing, nor is any loss or violence inflicted on them by it
edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII; Wiesbaden: Sändig 1969 reissue
what_it_says: Intelligent (spiritual) natures are not harmed by the resurrection of men, because it does not hinder them and does not touch them.
use: context for the angelology of the Legatio (Leg. 24 'multitude of angels'): the work speaks of a class of non-human intelligent beings, with no Son or Spirit named
limits: Athenagoras does not say what these beings are; identification with angels comes only from Otto's apparatus (A7-03). No Christological or Trinitarian statement.

ref: ch. 10, Otto apparatus note on νοηταὶ φύσεις (Otto's own commentary, not Athenagoras)
greek: Latin note (OCR): "Vocantur νοηταὶ φύσεις … procul dubio angeli (daemones a Gentilibus vocati), ab initio immortales ac sine fine perdurantes" (Greek lemma as printed by Otto)
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, apparatus on the same printed page as A7-02 (PDF p. 435). Text layer OCR; the ellipsis marks lines I did not transcribe. Latin commentary, not a Greek quotation from Athenagoras.
english: Not translated. Gloss: Otto takes νοηταὶ φύσεις to be angels (or Gentile 'daemones'), immortal from the beginning and everlasting.
translator: own gloss (Latin read by me; not a translation of a text Athenagoras wrote)
edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII; Wiesbaden: Sändig 1969 reissue
what_it_says: The editor's note identifies the 'spiritual natures' of ch. 10 with angels and cross-refers to Supplicatio 10.
use: context for the angel passages (Leg. 24) — an editorial identification, not a claim of Athenagoras
limits: Editorial interpretation; it is not in Athenagoras' text. Says nothing of the Son or Spirit.

ref: ch. 12 (Otto '12.' marker; ANF ch. 12 'Argument for the Resurrection from the Purpose...')
greek: Ἔστι δὲ ὁ μὲν ἀπὸ τῆς αἰτίας λόγος, ἐὰν ἐπισκοπώμεν πότερον ἁπλῶς καὶ μάτην γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος τινος ἕνεκεν
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 443 (printed p. 230, running head visible). Line break 'ἐπισκοπώ--μὲν'; OCR 'Ἵπότερον' read as πότερον.
english: The argument from the cause will appear, if we consider whether man was made at random and in vain, or for some purpose
what_it_says: One way to argue for the resurrection is from the cause of human creation: was man made for a purpose?
use: context (argument from purpose; God the Creator, no Son or Logos as agent)
limits: Here 'the Creator' is the subject of the purpose argument; the text does not name a second divine person.

ref: ch. 15 (Otto marks 'C. 15' cross-reference on p. 222; ANF ch. 15 'Argument ... from the Nature of Man')
greek: Εἰ δὲ καὶ νοῦς καὶ λόγος δέδοται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πρὸς διάκρισιν νοητῶν, οὐκ οὐσιῶν μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς τοῦ δόντος ἀγαθότητος καὶ σοφίας καὶ δικαιοσύνης, ἀνάγκη, διαμενόντων ὧν ἕνεκεν ἡ λογικὴ δέδοται κρίσις
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 477 (printed p. 248, running head visible). Line numbers '18' and '19' are Otto's. OCR 'ἀγα-ϑότητος' read as ἀγαθότητος.
english: And if both understanding and reason have been given to men for the discernment of things which
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2, 1885), newadvent.org/fathers/0206.htm (English fragment; the ANF sentence continues beyond it)
what_it_says: Human beings have νοῦς and λόγος (mind and reason) as faculties for discerning intelligible things; 'λόγος' here is a human faculty, not a divine person.
use: objection answered: a reader who finds 'νοῦς καὶ λόγος' in the Legatio (Leg. 10, Son as Father's νοῦς and λόγος) should see that the same pair is used here of man
limits: Does not say anything about the divine Logos; 'τοῦ δόντος' (the Giver) is not named. Not a Trinitarian text.

ref: ch. 18 (ANF ch. 18 'Judgment Must Have Reference Both to Soul and Body'; Greek paragraph located by content)
greek: ὡς γὰρ ἀγαϑὸς ὃ ποιητὴς ἡμῶν, οὕτω καὶ δίκαιος· ἀλόγεστος γὰρ ἣ ἄνευ δικαιοσύνης ἀγα-- ϑότης.
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 485 (printed p. 256, running head visible). Both lines in the text layer ('ὡς γὰρ ἀγαϑὸς ὃ ποιητὴς'; 'στος γὰρ ἣ ἄνευ δικαιοσύνης ἀγα--'); the middle words are from the djvu OCR. 'ἀλόγεστος' is an OCR reading of ἀλόγιστος-type text; kept as read.
english: the argument from rectitude, which represents God as judging men according as they have lived well or ill, derives its force from the end of their existence
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2, 1885), newadvent.org/fathers/0206.htm (paraphrase-level match: ANF does not render 'as good, so just' literally)
what_it_says: God the Maker is good and therefore also just; goodness without justice is unreasonable.
use: context: God as one Maker, good and just (no Son or Spirit)
limits: The Maker is 'ὃ ποιητής' (the Maker) without a second person; no Logos, no Trinity. The English is a paraphrase-level match.

ref: ch. 19 (ANF ch. 19 'Man Would Be More Unfavourably Situated Than the Beasts'; located by content)
greek: Εἰ γὰρ ἀφάτῳ προμηθείᾳ τοῦ πεποιηκότος ὑπὸ θεοῦ, καὶ δεῖ γε ταύτῃ τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλάσαντος διηνεκοῦς ἐπιμελείας ἀξιοῦσθαι
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 492 (printed p. 263, running head visible). 'EI:' in the text layer read as Εἰ.
english: But if the Maker of men takes any concern about His own works
what_it_says: If God the Maker has ineffable foresight and continuous care for what He made, He cares for man.
use: context: divine providence attributed to 'the Maker' (ποιητής/πλάσας) alone
limits: Only God the Maker is in view; the Greek contains no Logos, Son or Spirit.

ref: ch. 25 (end of the work; ANF ch. 25 'Argument Continued and Concluded')
greek: ταύτης γὰρ γενομένης καὶ τὸ τῇ φύσει τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρόσφορον ἐπακολουθεῖ τέλος. Τέλος δὲ [ζωῆς] ἔμφρονος καὶ λογικῆς
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 517 (printed p. 288, running head visible; continues on PDF 518 = p. 289). '[ζωῆς]' supplied from Otto's apparatus ('41. ζωῆς ἔμφρ. x. Aoy. κρ.'); marked as editor's restoration.
english: Nor again is it the happiness of soul separated from body: for we are not inquiring about the life or final cause of either of the parts of which man consists, but of the being who is composed of both
what_it_says: The argument ends by saying that the human being (soul and body together) has a fitting end, a life that is 'ἔμφρων καὶ λογικός' (thoughtful and rational).
use: context (ends with the human being, not a divine person)
limits: The final words 'ζωῆς ἔμφρονος καὶ λογικῆς' are partly restored; the English fragment is the nearest ANF sentence, not a line-by-line match.

ref: ch. 25 (PDF p. 517, earlier part of the same chapter)
greek: τὸ μὲν τέλος οὐχ ἁπλῶς, οὐδὲ τῶν ἐπιτυχόντων ἀνθρώπων, ὁ τῆς φύσεως τίθεται νόμος, ἀλλ᾽ αὐτῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κατὰ τὴν προλαβοῦσαν ζωὴν βεβιωκότων
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 517 (printed p. 288), text layer. OCR 'ξω.- nv' read as ζωὴν; 'βεβιῳκότων' read as βεβιωκότων.
english: there must be some appropriate end proposed for this life. But if it is the end of both parts together, and this can be discovered neither while they are still living in the present state of existence
what_it_says: The end of the human being is fixed by nature for those who lived in the earlier life, not for men at random.
use: context (human end; resurrection argued from the natural end of man)
limits: The argument concerns human persons, not God; no divine person is named.

ref: ch. 18 (Greek phrase on PDF p. 485; English ANF ch. 18 'superintendence of God')
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, PDF p. 485 (printed p. 256), text layer, fragment only; the words before it ('ἐκ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ') are from djvu OCR.
english: others, consequent upon the nature and the life of men, acquire their credibility from the superintendence of God over us
translator: B. P. Pratten (ANF vol. 2, 1885), newadvent.org/fathers/0206.htm (mapping by content, not by a literal match)
what_it_says: Some arguments for the resurrection depend on God's goodness as the Creator, who has given the present life.
use: context: God the Creator's goodness is the ground (no second divine person)
limits: Fragment only; the mapping to the ANF sentence is by content.

ref: title list in Otto's prolegomena (not a chapter)
greek: φιλοσόφου χριστιανοῦ περὲὸ ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν λόγος.
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, prolegomena title list, PDF p. 24 (printed page not read). OCR 'περὲὸ' = περὶ. Shows the manuscript title Περὶ ἀναστάσεως τῶν νεκρῶν with Ἀθηναγόρου Ἀθηναίου φιλοσόφου χριστιανοῦ.
what_it_says: The manuscripts give the title 'Athenagoras the Athenian, philosopher and Christian: On the resurrection of the dead'.
use: supports attribution (manuscript title); not an authenticity proof by itself
limits: Titles in manuscripts are secondary evidence; authorship debate is in notes.md. Title is not a quotation of the text.

ref: manuscript tradition (Otto prolegomena, Latin text with Greek title)
greek: Liber Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεχρῶν continetur tribus illis codicibus perantiquis (Par. 1. 2. Arg.) … Codex a Baane notario Aretae archiepiscopi Caesariensis, anno Christi 914 exaratus est.
greek_edition: Otto 1857 vol. VII, prolegomena, PDF p. 18 (text layer, OCR). Latin commentary with Greek title; read as OCR.
english: Not translated. Gist: the De resurrectione is contained in the most ancient manuscripts (Parisinus 1, 2 and Argentoratensis); Parisinus 451 (formerly 1169) was written in 914 by the notary Baanes for Archbishop Arethas.
page: prolegomena p. ~ii (page printed on PDF 18 not read); page unknown
what_it_says: The earliest manuscripts with the De resurrectione are from the 10th century (Paris gr. 451, 914), and they ascribe it to Athenagoras.
use: supports authenticity (manuscript ascription); the Paris codex date is the oldest witness
limits: Ascription is in manuscripts only; the Paris codex is the only one dated; no Christological content in this item.
